faqs.q: How much does a Canaan Dog cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Canaan Dog puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Canaan Dog, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Canaan Dogs due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Canaan Dog cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Canaan Dog are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Canaan Dogs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Yes — they are considered heavy shedders. Regular brushing is the most effective control tool. A slicker brush and undercoat rake are both essential for Canaan Dogs. Deshedding treatments from professional groomers can reduce seasonal shedding temporarily.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Canaan Dog need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Canaan Dog is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Canaan Dogs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Canaan Dogs easy to train?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Canaan Dogs. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Canaan Dogs commonly have?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs are most commonly associated with hip dysplasia. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Canaan Dogs live?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs have an average lifespan of 12–15 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Canaan Dogs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Canaan Dog puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Canaan Dog puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Canaan Dog-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Canaan Dogs good with kids?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs can be protective and may be cautious around unfamiliar children. Early socialisation with children from puppyhood significantly improves tolerance. Always supervise interactions between dogs and young children.

faqs.q: Do Canaan Dogs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Canaan Dogs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Canaan Dogs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Canaan Dog need per day?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Canaan Dogs good running partners?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Canaan Dog doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Canaan Dog be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Canaan Dog depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A long-line is recommended as an intermediate step for several months.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: A Canaan Dog needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Adult Canaan Dogs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Canaan Dogs do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Canaan Dog from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Canaan Dogs can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Canaan Dog a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Canaan Dogs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Canaan Dogs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Canaan Dogs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Canaan Dog?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Canaan Dog — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
